procedures.title: Fiberglass repair precautions
steps: Use the protective cream whenever working with Resin Kit materials; it is generally not needed with the plastic solder kit.
Wash hands and dry them completely.
Put about 1/2 inch (1/2 teaspoon) of #71 cream in the palm.
Spread it thinly until it vanishes, working it into cuticles, between the fingers and around the wrists.
Apply a second coat the same way (repeat the squeeze and spread steps).
Briefly hold hands under cold running water to set the cream.
Get resin mix off your hands quickly, and always before it begins to gel; clean it off with lacquer thinner, then soap and water.
Wear a respirator when grinding; rinse skin in cold water to reduce irritation from glass and cured resin dust.
Where possible, use a belt sander fitted with a vacuum attachment to control dust.
Work only in a well ventilated area, since resin mixes can give off toxic fumes.
Keep resin off clothing.
Use only the approved repair kits; other materials may not meet engineering and safety standards.
Keep materials, tools and the work area clean and dry, because dirt or moisture can upset the chemical reaction.
Before repairing, press around the damage by hand to find hidden hairline cracks or breaks.
Also inspect other likely spots (around exhaust pipes, grille, headlamps and wear points) for minor damage and fix it early.
notes: Cream protects against contact (occupational) dermatitis, which is not contagious; improved resin formulas in the approved kits have nearly eliminated skin irritation.

procedures.title: Plastic solder kit repair (minor damage)
steps: Strip the finish from the damaged spot with paint remover or a power sander, and check for other areas needing repair.
Mix the materials (see figure 56 in the manual).
Spread the material with a putty knife or rubber squeegee, working it into the damage and building it up to the required contour (see figure 57 in the manual).
For deep fills or vertical surfaces, build up in several layers of about 1/2 inch each.
Grind, sand and paint as usual to finish (see figure 58 in the manual).

specs.what: max layer thickness, deep or vertical fills

notes: For small cracks, surface flaws and small holes.

procedures.title: Resin kit repair (major damage)
steps: Press by hand around the damage to find hidden damage.
Strip the finish around the damage with paint remover, then inspect again for more damage.
Grind or file a "V" into the crack or break, giving the sides of the V a shallow slope for the most bonding area; a belt sander with vacuum attachment keeps dust down (see figure 59 in the manual).
If the back of the damage can be reached, plan a button-type repair: clean the back side so resin-soaked glass cloth can be laminated on both sides.
Cut the fiberglass cloth to size, at least five layers for a typical repair.
Mix hardener and resin at 1 part hardener to 4 parts resin, adding Thixatrope to thicken the mix and cut down on runniness.
notes: Kit contains resin, hardener, Thixatrope, fiberglass cloth, protective creams and mixing utensils; used for torn panels and separated joints.
Caution (continues next page): cleanliness is critical.
